messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: Digg.com
parts:
Thanks for the heads up! It looks like the server is fine, but the app isn't doing so well, because Shiny Server currently starts a single R process for each app, which is shared across all client sessions. Once we update Shiny Server to start a new R process for every N client sessions, it should be able to handle traffic spikes like this much better!

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: Digg.com
parts:
A quick note about Andrew Clark's TV show app - we helped him optimize it so that it could handle the load from digg (about 80 simultaneous connections at the peak). It's a reminder that one needs to consider new issues when an app goes from just a handful of simultaneous users to dozens or hundreds.

We'll post more about the specific changes we made, since that information will be useful for many others, I'm sure.

-Winston

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: Digg.com
parts:
Thanks for the reminder - here are the main changes we made to improve performance:

The primary bottleneck for Andrew's app was that, each time someone wanted to view data for a show, it fetched the data from a remote website, which was not particularly fast. This was fine for just a few simultaneous users, but not for digg-scale traffic. There were two things we did to help speed it up:

 - Installed the memoise package and, and use it to cache the download results for each show/URL. The memoized function was defined _outside_ of the shinyServer() call, so that the cache is shared across all user sessions (see the Scoping section of the tutorial for more info). For more about using memoise, see https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups=#!searchin/shiny-discuss/memoise/shiny-discuss/GPdLbZEN45s/rBcRv9uztYsJ.  

 - Although memoization speeds things up, the cache persists only within a R session, so it is lost whenever the app quits or crashes. Unfortunately, crashes happened frequently, due to (A) a bug in shiny server (which is now fixed) and (B) a problem in making plots with extended characters (worked around). Instead of downloading data for each show whenever the app restarted, we wrote a script to download all the data and save it in a subdirectory of the app. After this, the app simply loaded data from local files, so even after a crash, it was fast.


Andrew's app also exposed a bug in selectInput when the same name is shared with more than one choice (fixed):
  https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/157


In general, as the traffic to an app increases, you'll want to cache results and shift more of the work to be done ahead of time, before the user visits. The kinds of things you'll want to handle this way include expensive computations and slow network transfers. If traffic is very high, it might also help to pre-render images, save them, and send them with renderImage(), instead of using renderPlot().

-Winston
